main_text.p: πίγγων αὐτοῖς εἰσιν αἱ μάςιγες, ἃς ἀποκτυπῶσιν εἰς τὴν αἰ-θέρα, καὶ τύμπανα φειχώδη[?] πινὰ[?] δόμβον ἐξ ἑαυτῶν ἀνιέντα: Tu-bis Indi non vtuntur, sed pro iis sunt Flagella, quæ excu-tiunt in aërem, & tympana item, horribilem quemdam bombum emittentia. Inuenio Abaros quoque, gentem barbaram (Hunos alij vocant) habuisse. MenanderEt Abari. historicus: Οἱ δὲ ἄβαροι[?] κατὰ τὴν τῶ πολέμω κίνησιν ἐκ-λοντο ἦχον ἐγεῖραι ξυμμιγῆ τε καὶ ἄγελον, ἐπὶ τὲ ἂν ξὺν τῶ ἀλλαγματῶ ἐπιδέδεται[?] ταῖς τυμπάνοις: Abari initio præ-lij statuerant excitare mixtum quemdam & ferum sonum, simulque cum barritu persnare tympanis. Cuiusmodi tamen hæc tympana, haud probè scio: & à nostris certè diuersa illa Indorum. Nam in Suidâ describuntur: exTympana Indorumqualia? palmæ arboris cauato stipite, cui tintinnabula ex orichalco introrsus adaptabant, & os deinde vasi taurino corio occludebant: atque id in altum ferebant, concutiebántque in acie. Tintinnabula igitur, quæ multa & magna intus, incoditum quemdam sonum edebant. Plutarchus ParthosEt Parthis talis. quoque facit non cornibus, aut tubis incitare se ad pugnam: ἀλλὰ, inquit, ῥόπτεσ βυρσοπαγῆ καὶ κοῖλα πεςτει-In Crasso. ναντες ἡχείοις χαλκοῖς ἅμα πολλαχόθεν ἀπὸ πέσοι[?]. τὰ δὲ φθέγγεται βύτιόν τι καὶ δεινὸν, ὠρυγῇ θηλώδη[?] καὶ τραχύτητι βεβρυτῆς μεμιγμένον: sed stipites quosdam corio tectos & concauos tintinnabulis æreis circumpositis plurifariam simul pulsant. Illi verò obscurum aliquid & terribile resonant, ex vlulatu ferino & tonitru commixtum. page.notes: Left margin shows fragments of the facing page's text, excluded. Greek passages are read from a small, partly worn print; words marked [?] are doubtful, especially φειχώδη, πινὰ, ἄβαροι, ἐπιδέδεται, πέσοι and θηλώδη. The Greek in the first line is cut off at the left edge of the text block. Italic/roman distinction is approximate in places. Printed line "ctum" begins after "induĉ-" at the line break, and the words "similiter" in the middle of the paragraph do not appear on the page and are an error of the transcription; the correct reading at that point is "indu-ctum" with no extra word.
